metadata.title: Bullion Sales Tax in Kentucky (2026): Rules, Exemptions & Examples

description: Kentucky has statewide sales tax, but investment gold/silver bullion and covered coins are fully exempt. Jewelry is taxable. No threshold applies.

What's covered by the exemption
Gold/silver bullion and certain coins held for investment
How they decide what counts as bullion
The state asks whether the item is priced for its metal value (qualifying bullion) or for rarity, design, or collector demand (taxable).
What's NOT covered
Jewelry, rarity-priced collectibles, paper currency held as collectible, fabricated/industrial-use precious metal, and accessories.
Common questions about sales tax on gold and silver in Kentucky.
Is gold and silver bullion taxable in Kentucky?
+
No. Kentucky exempts bullion when it is treated as an investment item under the state’s investment-hold approach.
Are bullion coins exempt in Kentucky?
+
Certain coins held for investment are exempt along with bullion, while non-investment collectibles may not qualify.
Are numismatic coins taxed in Kentucky?
+
It depends. Kentucky’s exemption centers on investment bullion and covered investment-held coins, so collectible pieces outside that scope can be taxable.
Is jewelry subject to Kentucky sales tax?
+
Yes. Jewelry is taxable even when investment bullion and covered coins are exempt.
Is there a minimum purchase amount for Kentucky’s bullion exemption?
+
No. The provided rules do not include a dollar threshold for the bullion exemption.
